newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF set to review Russian economic performance.
newsitem.headline: IMF set to review Russian economic performance.

text.p: A team of experts from the International Monetary Fund arrived in Moscow on Monday for its regular monthly review of the Russian economy, chief representative Thomas Wolf said.
But Wolf said the mission, which is reviewing figures from the end of August, was likely to stay just a few days.
Issues which could not be dealt with this week could be discussed at the annual IMF meeting, which is due to take place in Washington in early October, he added.

The IMF has backed Russia's economic reforms with a $10 billion three-year loan. It delayed one tranche of the loan during the summer because of concern about lower than forecast tax revenues, but handed the money over last month.
The IMF paid another $350 million tranche to Russia last week and said Russian reforms were still on track.
An IMF spokesman said the Fund's board was pleased that Moscow was pushing ahead with structural economic reforms after slow progress in the first half of this year.
Economists said low tax collection was likely to be the main problem facing the IMF at this month's review as well.
"Russia is still a long way from serious tax reform," said Charles Blitzer, chief economist, emerging markets, with Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette in London.
Russia, which launched its economic reform programme in January 1992, has brought inflation down sharply in the last 12 months, but there is no sign yet of a lasting economic recovery.
August gross domestic product is still eight percent below year-ago levels, although it rose five percent from July.
Consumer prices fell 0.2 percent in August, after a rise of 0.7 percent in July.
